cards.text: Judah has a brand new king in Jerusalem, and his name is Manasseh. And friend, this king is YOUNG. I bet that crown is sliding right down over his eyebrows.

cards.question: How old is Manasseh when he becomes king of Judah?
Young king, LONG run. Manasseh reigns in Jerusalem for ___ years.

cards.text: Manasseh does evil in the sight of the LORD, copying the abominations of the nations the LORD drove out before the Israelites. Friend, that's flipping past every good recipe card to the one with ABOMINATION written across the top and saying, "Ooh, let's make THIS one."

cards.question: Manasseh's father, King Hezekiah, had torn down the high places. Manasseh ___ them.
Along with the high places, Manasseh raises up altars for the Baals and makes Asherah poles.

cards.text: He worships and serves all the host of heaven too. Then he builds altars in the LAST place on earth you'd ever expect.

cards.question: Where does Manasseh build altars to all the host of heaven?

answers.text: In both courtyards of the LORD's house
On the slopes of the Mount of Olives

cards.text: This is the very house of which the LORD had said, “My Name will remain in Jerusalem forever.” Friend, I get nervous when a baker moves my sprinkles ONE shelf over, and this man is building altars in God's house!
It gets darker, friend. He sacrifices his sons in the fire in the Valley of Ben-hinnom.

cards.question: Through all of this, Manasseh stays far away from sorcery, mediums and spiritists.

cards.text: He does great evil in the sight of the LORD, provoking Him to anger. Then he takes the carved image he made and sets it up in the house of God.

cards.question: God had promised David and Solomon He would never again make the Israelites leave their land. But there was a condition. What was it?

answers.text: That they carefully do all He commanded through Moses
That they build Him a bigger and grander temple
That they defeat every nation living around them

cards.question: Manasseh leads Judah and Jerusalem astray, until they do ___ evil than the nations the LORD destroyed before the Israelites.

cards.text: So the LORD speaks to Manasseh and his people, and they don't listen. I ignored a beeping oven timer ONE time, friend, and I'm still scraping that tray.

cards.question: Since Manasseh and his people won't listen, the LORD brings the military commanders of Egypt's king against them.

cards.text: The commanders of Assyria's king capture Manasseh, put a hook in his nose and bind him with bronze shackles. I spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer, friend, and even I never had a hook in my mustache.

cards.question: Where do the Assyrian commanders take King Manasseh?

cards.text: King Manasseh is a long way from his throne in Jerusalem now, and he is in distress. Friend, I know that spot: at the bottom of the drawer, there's only one way left to look.

cards.question: In his distress, Manasseh seeks the favor of the LORD his God and earnestly ___ himself before the God of his fathers.
After everything Manasseh has done, the LORD receives his plea and hears his prayer.
The LORD hears Manasseh's plea. Where does the LORD bring him?

answers.text: Back to Jerusalem and his kingdom
To a quiet house in Babylon

cards.question: Home again in Jerusalem, what does Manasseh come to know?

answers.text: That his army had saved him
That his idols had rescued him

cards.text: After this, Manasseh rebuilds the outer wall of the City of David, raises it much higher and stations military commanders in the fortified cities of Judah. Same man who rebuilt the high places, and NOW he's rebuilding the right stuff!

cards.question: Next Manasseh turns to the house of the LORD, still holding the foreign gods and the idol he put there. What does he do with them?

answers.text: He dumps them outside the city
He moves them into his palace
He hides them in the courtyards

cards.text: The altars he built on the temple mount and in Jerusalem go out the door too. Then he restores the altar of the LORD and sacrifices peace offerings and thank offerings on it.

cards.question: With the altar of the LORD restored, what does Manasseh tell the people of Judah?

answers.text: To serve the LORD the God of Israel
To bring their idols to the palace

cards.question: Once Manasseh tells Judah to serve the LORD, the people stop sacrificing at the high places.

cards.text: They still sacrifice at the high places, but only to the LORD their God. Half-fixed, friend, like a cookie that's golden on top and still gooey in the middle.

The rest of Manasseh's story, with his prayer and the words of the seers who spoke to him, is written in the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel. The Records of the Seers hold it too: his prayer, his sin and every place he set up high places and idols before he humbled himself.

cards.question: When Manasseh rests with his fathers, where is he buried?

cards.text: Manasseh's son Amon reigns in his place, and he's twenty-two when he becomes king. Now the BIG question, friend: which half of his dad's story is this young man going to copy?

cards.question: Amon reigns in Jerusalem for ___ years.
Amon does evil like his father, serving and sacrificing to all the idols Manasseh had made. And like his father, Amon humbles himself before the LORD.

cards.text: Instead, Amon increases his guilt. His dad left him the greatest comeback story in the kingdom, and he only copied the FIRST half.

cards.question: King Amon's own servants conspire against him. What do they do?

answers.text: They kill him in his palace
They hand him over to Assyria
They drive him out of Jerusalem

cards.question: The people of the land let the servants who conspired against King Amon go free.
The people of the land make Amon's son ___ king in his place.
